title: Operator entitlement fingerprinting, audit-fencekeeper, and KMS geo-fanout
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds operator entitlement fingerprinting to prevent lateral privilege expansion, deploys an audit-fencekeeper service that enforces log consistency for jurisdictional events, and introduces a KMS geo-fanout router with affinity scoring. Backwards-compatible; opt-in via feature flag and gradual rollout to prod clusters.
description: Motivation: Recent audits and a support incident (SUP-1123) showed a gap in how operator sessions were attributed when requests traversed region-linked proxies. That made post-incident forensics and residency claims brittle. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) entitlement fingerprinting: compute a stable, short-lived fingerprint for operator sessions that binds operator identity, session nonce, source geozone, and service boundary to prevent silent operator impersonation or replay across regions; 2) audit-fencekeeper: a gate that ensures audit logs for jurisdiction-sensitive operations are written with canonical metadata and blocks a request path unless an immutable audit envelope is produced; 3) KMS geo-fanout router: when multiple KMS providers are available, route encryption operations with an affinity score based on tenant residency, operator geozone, and cost heuristics with safe fallbacks. Design notes: Entitlement fingerprinting is generated at the auth proxy layer and propagated as X-Ent-Fingerprint header. Fingerprints are HMAC-SHA256 over (operator_id|session_id|source_zone|service_scope|timestamp_window) with a short TTL and rotation at the proxy. The fencekeeper intercepts audit writes and verifies the presence of the fingerprint and a signed audit-seal before allowing side-effects for region-pinned resources. KMS geo-fanout uses a policy engine: candidate providers are scored by residency match (+100), low-latency bump (+30), and cost delta penalty (-cost_weight*delta). The router falls back deterministically to the next available provider while annotating audit metadata with the decision vector. Implementation summary: commits: - create entitlement fingerprint generator and validation hooks in auth-proxy (auth-proxy/*) - add audit-fencekeeper service with gRPC ingress and enforcement middleware (audit/fencekeeper/*) - wire fencekeeper checks into resource controllers for tenancy-sensitive writes (controllers/tenancy/*) - add KMS routing layer and policy config (kms/router.go, config/kms-policies.yaml) - add unit and integration tests and a small e2e harness that simulates cross-region operator hops (tests/e2e/geo-ops) Files changed (high level): auth-proxy/pkg/fingerprint.go (new), auth-proxy/middleware.go (hook), audit/fencekeeper/service.go (new), audit/fencekeeper/middleware.go (new), controllers/tenancy/handler.go (patch), kms/router.go (new), config/kms-policies.yaml (new), tests/e2e/geo-ops/test_geo_handoff.go (new), ci/workflows/audit-fencekeeper-integration.yaml (new), docs/security/entitlement-fingerprint.md (new). Small illustrative snippet: in auth-proxy/pkg/fingerprint.go we compute the fingerprint as: hmac := HMAC_SHA256(master_key, fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%s|%s|%d", operatorID, sessionID, zone, scope, window)) The fencekeeper API is light-weight: VerifyEnvelope(request_id, fingerprint, envelope) returns (ok,bool, reason,string). Rollout and migration: guarded behind feature flag feature.entitlement_fingerprint. Default off for all prod clusters. Rollout plan: stage 1 - land feature flag and non-blocking fencekeeper that emits metrics and logs only (canary namespace) 2 weeks. stage 2 - enable fencekeeper enforcement for a small cohort of tenants (10%) and monitor audit write latency and error rates. stage 3 - broad enforcement once we see stable metrics and no regression in latency SLOs. Metrics and alarms: new grafana dashboards and alerts included for: audit_fencekeeper_reject_rate, entitlement_fp_generation_failures, kms_router_fallback_rate, audit_write_latency_p50/p95. Thresholds: reject_rate > 0.1% for 1h triggers paging. Testing: unit tests added for HMAC edge cases and spoof attempts; integration test simulates operator hop from eu-west to us-east and verifies envelope rejection when fingerprint mismatches. Security review notes: keying material for HMAC uses the existing operator master key stored in KMS and rotates via the key-rotation pipeline; fencekeeper stores minimal envelope metadata and leverages existing audit-retention pipes to avoid duplication. Performance: benchmark of fingerprint generation adds ~120μs at auth-proxy median; fencekeeper adds ~2ms to audit-call path in our canary cluster. These numbers are within SLO but we'll watch after ramp. Review conversation (abridged): Nina Gupta: "Can we ensure the fingerprint doesn't leak PII and that it's deterministic across proxies?" Aisha: "Yes the fingerprint is derived from IDs and a time window; no raw user names or emails are included. Documentation updated to call this out." Thomas Wang: "What happens if KMS routing fails for all providers?" Aisha: "Router will return a deterministic 5xx and fencekeeper will block the side-effect. We document fallback and add a retry/backoff in router; incident runbook updated." Liam O'Connor: "Suggest adding a metric for the decision vector histogram." Aisha: "Done - added kms_router_decision_vector metric and tagged logs for replay." CI: go unit tests pass, integration workflow ran against staging and passed with one transient flake retried. Lint and security-scanner flagged a missing input validation in controllers/tenancy/handler.go which was fixed in a follow-up commit. Backwards compatibility and opt-out: existing clients that do not send X-Ent-Fingerprint are compatible while fencekeeper runs in observation mode. When enforcement is enabled, operator sessions without a valid fingerprint will be rejected with 403 and an explicit error code (ERR_AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_MISSING) with guidance to rotate clients. Related work: ENG-3219 (operator session hardening), ENG-4987 (kms router policy engine) Linear tickets mentioned above. Merge notes: feature gated, merged via squash, and feature flag default off. Post-merge actions: - schedule canary rollout in nimbus-prod cluster starting 2026-03-02 - add dashboard panels to incident book and notify security on the 10% cohort flip - run a small compliance validation against tenants in EU region to verify residency enforcement. Known limitations and follow-ups: - current fingerprint window is conservative; future work may permit per-tenant TTL tuning - we do not yet export a global audit-proof index; planned follow-up ENG-4041 - additional KMS cost tuning to be addressed by finance pairing on ENG-5232.
